panels.title: A — Bill total vs InfluxDB-projected total
panels.description: Per-cycle bill total ($) compared with a forward-projected estimate from InfluxDB (Refoss whole-home W * ComEd hourly price, integrated over the bill window). v1: only the Bill series is real; the Projected series is a documented stub returning zero — implementation deferred until several cycles of data accumulate.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "energy")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "comed.bill" and r._field == "total_due" and r.bill_type == "normal")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> yield(name: "Bill")

panels.title: B — EAGLE kWh vs billed kWh per cycle
panels.description: Bill-side kWh per cycle. Compare against EAGLE meter integration over the same window to validate the meter is reading what the utility is billing.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "energy")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "comed.bill" and r._field == "kwh" and r.bill_type == "normal")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> yield(name: "Billed kWh")

panels.title: D — Capacity charge tracker
panels.description: Peak kW (locked annually from prior summer's PJM 5CP) and the resulting Capacity Charge line item per bill. The HVAC scheduler exists primarily to suppress this peak.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "energy")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "comed.bill" and r._field == "peak_kw")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> yield(name: "Peak kW")

from(bucket: "energy")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "comed.bill_lineitems" and r.line_item == "Capacity Charge" and r._field == "amount")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> yield(name: "Capacity Charge ($)")

panels.title: F — Forward projection (current cycle)
panels.description: v1: shows the most recent bill total. The full forward-projection formula (supply-so-far + delivery estimate + capacity + taxes estimate + days-remaining extrapolation) is sketched in the design doc and lands as a follow-on after a few cycles of real data accumulate.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "energy")
  |> range(start: -90d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "comed.bill" and r._field == "total_due" and r.bill_type == "normal")
  |> last()
